items.followUp: How can water be changed from a liquid into a gas?

rubric.why: Temperature and pressure can cause a change of state.
rubric.description: States that matter can be changed from one state to another by changing temperature or pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying either temperature or pressure as a way to change state.

rubric.why: Gives a relevant example of changing the conditions to produce a change of state.
rubric.description: Gives an example of changing temperature or pressure to change a state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as heating, cooling, or changing pressure.

modelAnswer: Matter can be changed from one state to another by changing its temperature or pressure.
For example, heating a liquid can change it into a gas.

items.followUp: Derive the second equation of motion using a velocity-time graph.

rubric.why: The graph represents the initial and final velocities over the time interval.
rubric.description: Draws and labels a velocity-time graph with initial velocity u, final velocity v, and time t.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly labelled velocity-time graph.

rubric.why: The area under the graph gives displacement.
rubric.description: Uses the area of the trapezium under the graph to write the displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct area expression.

rubric.why: This relates acceleration, change in velocity, and time.
rubric.description: Uses the acceleration relation to express v or t.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct acceleration relation.

rubric.why: This is the required third equation of motion obtained by eliminating time.
rubric.description: Eliminates t and obtains the third equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final equation.

modelAnswer: Draw a velocity-time graph with initial velocity u at t = 0 and final velocity v at time t; the area under the graph represents displacement s.
The area of the trapezium gives s = 1/2 (u + v)t.
From acceleration, a = (v − u)/t, so t = (v − u)/a.
Substitute t: s = (u + v)(v − u)/(2a).
Therefore, 2as = v² − u², and v² = u² + 2as.

items.followUp: A 0.4 kg body moves at 5 m s⁻¹ in a circle of radius 2 m. Find the centripetal force.

rubric.why: Correctly identifies the mass, radius, and speed, including converting centimetres to metres.
rubric.description: Writes the given data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for all three correct values in SI units.

rubric.why: Uses the centripetal-force relation.
rubric.description: States the correct formula for centripetal force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Substitutes the given values correctly.
rubric.description: Substitutes the SI values into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution.

rubric.why: The calculation gives the required force, expressed in newtons.
rubric.description: Calculates and states the centripetal force with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for 4.5 N; award 1 mark if the numerical result is correct but the unit is missing.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 0.5 kg, r = 50 cm = 0.5 m, v = 3 m s⁻¹.
Formula: F = mv²/r.
Substitution: F = (0.5 kg)(3 m s⁻¹)²/(0.5 m).
F = 4.5 kg m s⁻² = 4.5 N.

items.followUp: State the second condition of equilibrium and explain its meaning.

rubric.why: A body in equilibrium has no resultant effect causing a change in its motion.
rubric.description: Defines equilibrium as a state in which a body is at rest or moves with uniform velocity.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the definition; award 1 mark for mentioning either rest or uniform velocity.

rubric.why: The first condition is zero resultant force.
rubric.description: States the first condition of equilibrium mathematically or in words.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the vector sum of forces is zero.

rubric.why: Zero resultant force means there is no linear acceleration.
rubric.description: Explains that the first condition ensures translational equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the condition to zero linear acceleration or translational equilibrium.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when it is at rest or moves with uniform velocity, with no acceleration.
The first condition of equilibrium is that the vector sum of all forces acting on the body is zero: ΣF = 0.
This means the body has no linear acceleration and is in translational equilibrium.

items.followUp: A wire of length 2 m and cross-sectional area 1 × 10⁻⁶ m² extends by 1 × 10⁻³ m under a force of 20 N. Find its Young's modulus.

accept: ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain
rubric.why: Young's modulus is defined as the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain.
rubric.description: Defines Young's modulus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition, with the elastic-limit condition stated or understood.

rubric.why: These expressions give the stress and strain used in the derivation.
rubric.description: Writes the stress and strain relations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly expressing stress and strain.

rubric.why: Substituting stress and strain gives the required formula.
rubric.description: Derives the formula for Young's modulus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining Y = FL/(AΔL).

rubric.why: Young's modulus has the same SI unit as stress.
rubric.description: States the SI unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for N m⁻² or pascal (Pa).

modelAnswer: Young's modulus is the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain, provided the material is within its elastic limit.
Tensile stress = F/A, and tensile strain = ΔL/L.
Y = tensile stress/tensile strain = (F/A)/(ΔL/L) = FL/(AΔL).
Its SI unit is N m⁻², also called the pascal (Pa).

items.followUp: Define uniform motion and give one example.

rubric.why: Rest is described by an unchanged position relative to the surroundings.
rubric.description: Describes the position of a body at rest relative to its surroundings.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its position does not change with respect to its surroundings.

rubric.why: Motion is described by a changing position relative to the surroundings.
rubric.description: Describes the position of a body in motion relative to its surroundings.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its position changes with respect to its surroundings.

modelAnswer: A body is at rest if its position does not change with respect to its surroundings.
A body is in motion if its position changes with respect to its surroundings.
